payload.text: Check whether the adolescent waitlist study answers the adult attention-control question.
Look for a permitted methods or adverse-event report for A1; keep unsupported details unknown.

sources.body: Study abstract (simulated data). In a simulated randomized study of 80 adults with depression, 40 received cognitive behavioural therapy and 40 received attention control. At six weeks, response occurred in 18 of 40 versus 12 of 40 participants; the risk-difference interval was -4 to 34 percentage points. Adverse events and subgroup outcomes were not reported in this abstract.

sources.body: Study abstract (simulated data). A separate simulated randomized study assigned 50 adults with depression to cognitive behavioural therapy and 50 to attention control. At six weeks, response occurred in 20 of 50 versus 21 of 50 participants. The authors reported no clear difference between groups.
